correctness.rationale: For the normalized kernel Gram matrix with data inner product N^-1 sum, the Fourier eigenvalues are precisely the N Poisson-congruence masses. This gives Q=1/min p. A finite alias cutoff plus Stirling two-sided mass bounds yields p_min~N^-1/2 exp(-N max_t min_l J_rho(t+l)) up to constant factors for fixed rho. J(x+1)-J(x)=log(B(x)/rho), B strictly increasing, forces one transition at rho=e^-1 and the identric tie for rho>e^-1. The boundary alias k=0 is handled separately and the selected minimizer has strictly positive asymptotic arguments, sustaining the sqrt(N) prefactor. Independent Python log-sum-exp checks at N=400 and rho=.1,e^-1,.5,1,2,3 produced rates and residues consistent with the claimed branches, not a proof of all N.
